learn.hook: What is your biggest wish? Is wishing enough, or do you need to do something more?
points: The lesson 'Madhu's Wish' is about a child's wish, hard work and family.
A wish is something you really want to happen.
Many wishes come true with hard work and practice.
If you fall or fail, do not give up. Try again!

example.q:
Read:
Tara wished she could ride a bicycle like her big brother, Dev. Every evening, she put on her helmet and practised in the lane while Papa held the seat. She fell many times, but she did not give up. 'Try again, beta,' said Dadi from the steps. After two weeks, Papa let go, and Tara rode all by herself! The whole family clapped and cheered.
How did Tara's wish come true?
steps: Find what Tara wished for: to ride a bicycle.
Find what she did: she practised every evening and did not give up when she fell.
Her practice helped her ride by herself.
example.answer: Her wish came true because she practised every day and did not give up.

learn.reallife: Learning to swim, to skip rope or to write neatly all need practice. Each try makes you better!

games.title: Story order
items: Tara wished to ride a bicycle.
She fell, but did not give up.

games.title: Match the word to its meaning
pairs: do again and again to get better
a hard cap that keeps your head safe

quiz.q: The story begins: 'Tara wished she could ride a bicycle.' What was Tara's wish?
quiz.explain: The first sentence says Tara wished to ride a bicycle.
quiz.mistake: Guessed a wish instead of reading the first sentence

quiz.q: 'Tara wished she could ride a bicycle like her big brother, Dev.' Who is Dev?
quiz.explain: The sentence says 'her big brother, Dev'.
quiz.mistake: Did not read who Dev is

quiz.q: 'She practised in the lane while Papa held the seat.' Who held the seat?
quiz.explain: The sentence says Papa held the seat.
quiz.mistake: Mixed up the family members

quiz.q: 'She fell many times, but she did not give up.' What did Tara do after falling?
quiz.explain: 'Did not give up' means she kept trying.
quiz.mistake: Does not understand 'did not give up'

quiz.q: 'Try again, beta,' said Dadi from the steps. Who said these words?
quiz.explain: The words 'said Dadi' tell us the speaker.
quiz.mistake: Did not look at who spoke

quiz.q: 'After two weeks, Papa let go, and Tara rode all by herself!' How long did Tara practise before riding alone?
quiz.explain: The story says 'After two weeks'.
quiz.mistake: Did not read the time words in the story

quiz.q: Tara practised every day, fell many times and kept trying until she could ride. What does this story teach us?
options: Hard work and practice help wishes come true.
quiz.explain: Tara's practice made her wish come true.
quiz.mistake: Thinks wishing is enough

quiz.q: 'Every evening, she practised in the lane.' What does 'practised' mean?
options: did something again and again to get better
quiz.explain: To practise is to do something many times to get better at it.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of 'practise'

teach.ask: Gappu wishes he could fly high like the eagle. He asks: 'How can my wish come true?'
teach.praise: I will practise flying every day and never give up! Flap, flap!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me what Tara did to make her wish come true?

learn.hook: Who is in your family? Count them on your fingers!
points: Family words: mother, father, brother, sister, grandmother, grandfather, aunt, uncle, cousin.
Your father's mother is your Dadi, and your mother's mother is your Nani. Both are your grandmothers.
Your aunt's or uncle's children are your cousins.
In a joint family, grandparents, parents, uncles, aunts and cousins live together.
Families come in many sizes. Every family is special.

example.q: Who is your Bua, in English family words?
steps: Your parents' sisters are your aunts.
example.answer: Bua is my aunt (my father's sister).

learn.reallife: At a family wedding or festival, you meet chachas, mausis and cousins. Now you know their English names too!

items.text: My brother and I are our parents' ___.

quiz.q: Your father's mother is your ___.
quiz.explain: Your father's mother is your grandmother (Dadi).
quiz.mistake: Mixes up grandparents with aunts

quiz.q: Your mother's father is your ___.
quiz.explain: Your mother's father is your grandfather (Nana).
quiz.mistake: Mixes up grandfathers and uncles

quiz.q: Your aunt's son is your ___.
quiz.explain: The children of your aunts and uncles are your cousins.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a cousin is a brother

quiz.q: Your mother's sister is your ___.
quiz.explain: Your mother's sister is your aunt (Mausi).
quiz.mistake: Mixes up aunts with grandmothers

quiz.q: Your father's brother is your ___.
quiz.explain: Your father's brother is your uncle (Chacha or Tau).
quiz.mistake: Mixes up uncles with cousins

quiz.q: What is the plural of 'family'?
quiz.explain: Change y to ies: family – families.
quiz.mistake: Just adds -s

quiz.q: In which kind of family do grandparents, parents, uncles, aunts and cousins live together?
quiz.explain: When many members of a family live together, it is a joint family.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the term 'joint family'

quiz.q: Which of these is a family word?
quiz.explain: 'grandfather' names a family member.
quiz.mistake: Picks a naming word that is not a family member

teach.ask: Gappu met his mother's sister and his father's brother. He asks: 'What do I call them in English?'
teach.praise: Aunt and uncle! And their chicks are my cousins! Tweet!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me the English words for some family members?

learn.hook: Today Tara rides. Yesterday Tara... rode! Action words change when we talk about the past.
points: We use the past tense for things that have already happened.
Many action words add -ed: play – played, cheer – cheered, help – helped.
Some double the last letter: clap – clapped, stop – stopped. Some change y to ied: cry – cried.
Some do not add -ed. They change in a special way: go – went, eat – ate, ride – rode, fall – fell, see – saw.
Words like 'yesterday' and 'last week' tell us something happened in the past.

example.q: Change to the past: 'Tara rides her bicycle.' Start with 'Yesterday'.
steps: 'Yesterday' tells us it is the past.
'ride' does not add -ed. It changes to 'rode'.
So the sentence becomes 'Yesterday, Tara rode her bicycle.'

learn.reallife: When you tell your family what happened at school, you use the past tense: 'I played, I ate, I wrote.'

quiz.q: What is the past tense of 'play'?
quiz.explain: We add -ed: play – played.
quiz.mistake: Uses the present form instead of the past

quiz.q: What is the past tense of 'go'?
quiz.explain: 'go' changes fully to 'went'.
quiz.mistake: Adds -ed to a word that changes fully

quiz.q: Fill in: 'Yesterday, Tara ___ her bicycle.'
quiz.explain: 'Yesterday' tells us it is past, so we use 'rode'.
quiz.mistake: Does not use the clue word 'yesterday'

quiz.q: What is the past tense of 'fall'?
quiz.explain: 'fall' changes to 'fell'.
quiz.mistake: Adds -ed to 'fall'

quiz.q: What is the past tense of 'clap'?
quiz.explain: We double the 'p' and add -ed: clapped.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to double the last letter

quiz.q: What is the past tense of 'cry'?
quiz.explain: Change y to i and add -ed: cried.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to change y to i

quiz.q: Which sentence tells about the past?
quiz.explain: 'cheered' is the past tense, so it already happened.
quiz.mistake: Does not notice the -ed ending

quiz.q: Which word tells us something happened in the past?
quiz.explain: 'Yesterday' is the day before today, which is the past.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up past and future time words

teach.ask: Gappu wants to tell his mother about his day. He asks: 'How do I talk about things that already happened?'
teach.praise: Today I learnt the past tense. Yesterday I played and ate worms!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me how action words change when something already happened?
